data.title: BankUnited increases existing share buyback program by $150M
data.description:
• BankUnited (BKU) said on Thursday that its board has approved an additional $150 million authorization for the repurchase of its common stock under its existing share repurchase program.
  • The timing, number, and value of shares repurchased will depend on market conditions, capital requirements, legal and regulatory considerations, and other factors.
  • The board of directors may modify, suspend, extend, or terminate the share repurchase program at any time, the company said.

data.title: Bending Spoons rallies 7% after the close on Mailchimp deal
data.description:
Bending Spoons (BSP) shares rose more than 7% after the closing bell following the announcement of a deal to acquire Mailchimp for ~$3.68B. The consideration consists of $3.31B in cash and $368M in Bending Spoons' stock.

This followed a 3% dip during the session, with the stock finished at $41.70, down $1.09 on the day.

In addition, the digital-business acquirer said it agreed to sell 32.5 million ordinary shares in the private placement, with closing expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. Trading volume reached 4.26 million shares, and relative volume stood at 2.17.

data.title: Warby Parker sinks 14% as choppy trading continues
data.description:
Eyewear company Warby Parker (WRBY) dropped more than 14% on Wednesday. The stock finished at $24.13, falling $4.09 on the day.

The decline came as the broader market also fell. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF slipped almost 2%, and the consumer discretionary sector ETF lost almost 3%.

WRBY has seen choppy trading lately. The stock climbed nearly 9% on Wednesday following two straight days of losses. Shares also saw a drop of 11% on November 12, coming shortly after a rally of 19% on November 9.

data.title: Stocks making big moves after hours: INTU, BULL, GAP
data.description:
U.S. stocks ended significantly lower on Thursday as investors focused on the highly anticipated public debit of AI startup Anthropic (ANT).

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished -2.02%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) ended -2.25, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) finished -2.19%.

The biggest gainers on Thursday were Palo Alto Networks (PANW) +6.4%, Okta (OKTA) +5.7%, and Everpure (P) +4.7%.

The biggest losers were Williams-Sonoma (WSM) -15.2%, Twilio (TWLO) -8.8%, and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) -7.7%.

Here are stocks making moves after the market close:

  • Financial management and payment products company Intuit (INTU) closed -1% but slid more than 14% after the market close after the company reported Q1 earnings that met expectations but a full-year revenue guidance that was revised lower due to poor Credit Karma growth.
  • Webull Corp. (BULL) closed -2.14% on Thursday and declined further after market hours even after reporting beats in both revenue and EPS.
  • The retail giant Gap (GAP) ended -5.29% but jumped around 4% in after-hours trading as the company reported beats in EPS and revenue results that were in line with consensus.

data.title: Anthropic ascends into history with IPO; shares hit Nasdaq at $111.50
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) made history on Thursday as it became the first pure-play AI lab with a public listing on the Nasdaq (COMP:IND). Shares opened at $111.50.

Shares had declined to around $100 about an hour after public trading began, which was about 20% more than their initial pricing. The stock landed at $96.97 when the closing bell rang.

The Claude maker had priced its Class A common stock at $83. The opening price represented a surge of 33%. The offer comprised 980M shares, as Anthropic sold 956.35M shares, while certain existing stockholders sold 23.65M shares. At the IPO price, the combined offering raised approximately $81.34B, making it the largest IPO on record, surpassing SpaceX's $75B debut earlier this year.

The company reached a market capitalization of $2T in the opening moments of its IPO. This is well beyond the $1.4T that was expected in the days leading up to the offering.

Financial firms were already busy assigning ratings and price targets on the fresh stock. Needham initiated it at Buy with a $150 price target.

"Growth opportunities like ANT rarely come along, but we think history puts ANT in the same dominant bucket as fellow tech titans AMZN, GOOG, and MSFT," said Needham analyst Scott Berg in a Thursday investor note. "We believe ANT is the leading vendor in a rapidly growing AI market that could be 10% of the current $56T labor market. We think ANT's significant economies of scale and strong premium branding creates an edge in the highly competitive space, with Anthropic capable of investing tens of billions annually towards model training while driving premium profitability."

Amazon (AMZN) and Google (GOOG)(GOOGL) are both significant investors in Anthropic, holding stakes of 14.7% and 13.7%, respectively.

Needham expects Anthropic to experience 156% revenue growth in 2027 and 98% growth in 2028 along with 35%-plus operating margins and 90%-plus gross margins.

Citizens initiated the stock at Market Outperform with a $125 price target, and Melius assigned it a Buy rating and $155 target.

Anthropic beats OpenAI to IPO

With the IPO, Anthropic reached a major milestone ahead of its primary competitor, OpenAI (OPENAI), which is expected to go public in 2027. However, it hasn't been smooth sailing for Anthropic to reach this point. The recent drag on the tech sector has dramatically reduced its potential initial market cap. The tech-heavy Nasdaq has decreased about 10% over the past six weeks.

The listing comes at a tumultuous moment in the AI trade. 

"At a time in which investors are very nervous on the overall tech trade and the Nvidia (NVDA) black cloud moment casts a shadow over the tech sector, Anthropic's debut is a big near-term win for the tech sector and should help restore some investor confidence that the AI Revolution growth thesis is not waning," said analyst Dan Ives with Yorkville Ives in an investor note. "It is going through a very turbulent, white-knuckle period that does not change our longer-term view that $3 trillion to $4 trillion of capex will be spent over the next few years on the AI Revolution, and this sets the stage for the next phase of tech and infrastructure investment with Anthropic a central player in the buildout."

Government fallout 

Anthropic used to be the primary AI lab utilized by the U.S. military and various government agencies. This relationship unraveled in February 2026 as the company said it "cannot in good conscience" allow the Department of Defense to use its models in all lawful use cases without limitation.

This resulted in President Donald Trump demanding U.S. government agencies cut their existing ties with Anthropic. The U.S. also labeled the San Francisco-based company a supply-chain risk.

AI harkens doom and miracles

The capabilities of its ever-more-powerful AI models also generated serious concerns over elevated cybersecurity risks. Last month, JPMorgan (JPM) chief Jamie Dimon said that Anthropic's Mythos model has increased global cybersecurity risks tenfold.

Anthropic executives have also recently said its models have the potential to either destroy civilization within the next decade or fix many of its woes. Evan Hubinger, Alignment Science Lead at Anthropic, said in September he "earnestly" believes AI could kill all humans, putting his personal estimate of the probability at more than 10% within the next decade. Earlier this month, Amodei said widespread health issues such as cancer and mental illness might vanish within a decade due to the wonders of AI. 

"I think if we do this right, we can create an age of miracles where humanity is able to solve problems that have eluded us for millennia," he added.

Amodei, along with six other former OpenAI employees, founded Anthropic in January 2021. It released its first version of Claude to the public in March 2023, just months after OpenAI's ChatGPT hit the tech world. However, as OpenAI initially focused on consumer uses of AI, Anthropic targeted the enterprise and government sectors. Its release of Claude Code in 2025 propelled its revenue and reach, paving the path for its eventual IPO.
